title: A closed form solution for Bayesian analysis of a simple linear mixed model
summary: Linear mixed-effects models are a central analytical tool for modeling hierarchical and longitudinal data, as they allow simultaneous representation of fixed and random sources of variation. In practice, inference for such models is most often based on likelihood-based approximations, which are computationally efficient, but rely on numerical integration and may be unreliable example wise in small-sample settings.
